_provenance.subject: CRISPR gene editing
_provenance.source: Prism public API — research.evidence (one call per angle)
_provenance.note: Counts/shares computed in ClickHouse. Quoted findings verbatim and verified. Two angles fell to the subject lane (no clean both-sides intersection) and are reported that way, not charted by a both-sides count.

angles.claim: CRISPR gene editing can treat cancer
angles.reading: overwhelmingly positive framing, which on a citation-weighted corpus can mean consensus or can mean publication bias
angles.note: deepest lane, but concentrated in CAR-T immunotherapy and preclinical work; corpus_topics led by CAR-T cell therapy (46) and virus-based gene therapy (46)
evidence: CRISPR/Cas9-UCA1 knockdown significantly inhibited bladder-cancer cell proliferation, migration and invasion in vitro and in vivo (Oncotarget 2017, meta-analysis tier)

angles.claim: CRISPR gene editing has significant off-target effects
angles.reading: mostly positive framing, with a substantial cautionary minority
angles.note: the most contested CRISPR angle (29.9%) and the only one where the read document pushed back — newer methods report 'little or no' off-target editing
evidence: 'resulting in little or no undesirable on- or off-target effects' — dual-conditional CRISPR-Cas9 in human stem cells (Mol Ther Nucleic Acids 2022)
large deletions up to several thousand bases at Cas9 cut sites: HBB 11.7-35.4%, HBG 14.3%, BCL11A 13.2% (Sci Adv 2022)

angles.claim: CRISPR gene editing cures sickle cell disease
angles.note: the outcome pole resolved to MeSH only (Anemia, Sickle Cell), so no both-sides intersection formed and Prism fell back to the subject lane; the extracted health-claim layer carried the real evidence instead
evidence: 'both patients had ... transfusion independence, and (in the patient with SCD) elimination of vaso-occlusive episodes' — NEJM 2020, CRISPR-Cas9 for Sickle Cell Disease and β-Thalassemia (cited 1,856); single-arm, so the word 'cure' rests on uncontrolled data

angles.claim: CRISPR gene editing improves crop yield
angles.reading: overwhelmingly positive framing, which on a citation-weighted corpus can mean consensus or can mean publication bias
angles.lane_note: only 20 papers cover both sides of the claim; most CRISPR-crop work targets traits (disease resistance, quality), not yield itself, so the yield claim is thin at the claim level

angles.claim: base editing is more precise than CRISPR-Cas9
angles.lane_note: only 3 papers cover both sides of this comparison; the field describes base editing avoiding double-strand breaks and reporting 'no off-target mutations', but head-to-head precision benchmarks against CRISPR-Cas9 are almost absent — assumed, rarely demonstrated

stance_composition_pct.what: share of papers by stance toward the claim, normalised to 100%

research_per_year.what: research-index papers whose title carries the phrase 'CRISPR gene editing', by publication year, matched on Prism's live vocabulary (the broad topic 'CRISPR and Genetic Engineering' holds ~96,900 papers; this is the narrow title-phrase slice)

stance_trends.what: orientation framing of the CRISPR literature per year, 2017-2025; growth measured late-third vs early-third of the window

framing_shift.reading: the balance of framing is broadly unchanged

news.note: news on CRISPR is a thin, high-priority, almost-uniformly-positive stream; the qualifying/cautionary nuance lives in the research layer, not the news layer
news.geography_caveat: the place an article is ABOUT, not where published; only 43.3% of articles place cleanly, and acronym collisions inflate some low-count rows — directional, not precise

research_gaps.claim: CRISPR gene editing has significant off-target effects
components: off-target activity varies with guide-RNA design
significant off-target effects raise safety concerns
research_gaps.reading: the safety claim is fully scaffolded — a real literature behind every sub-claim, not a gap
